texts.text: 7 APPLICATIONS

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Segmentation is a starting point for many processes in image manipulation and computer vision. In the following we highlight several applications of our light field segmentation method.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: 7.1 User-guided Object Segmentation.
texts.text: 7.1 User-guided Object Segmentation.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Like most 2D and video segmentation methods, our method segments the light field into regions of consistent appearance, but not into semantic objects. However with a simple user interface, we can can manually select multiple regions that comprise a single object. Examples of this user-guided object segmentation are shown in Fig. 19.
texts.text: Like most 2D and video segmentation methods, our method segments the light field into regions of consistent appearance, but not into semantic objects. However with a simple user interface, we can can manually select multiple regions that comprise a single object. Examples of this user-guided object segmentation are shown in Fig. 19.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: 7.2 Light Field Flattening
texts.text: 7.2 Light Field Flattening

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Image flattening refers to the suppression of texture detail while preserving strong scene edges and overall image structure. Here, we extend an existing 2D method [Bi et al. 2015] to 4D. Specifically, we take into consideration the L 1 sparsity in spatial slices, angular patches as well as the 4D light field segmentation, and jointly minimize the pixel variation and approximation error as detailed in the following.
